name: UBO Identification Failure — Business Current Account Opening
journey_phase: BPH-001 through EX-B004 (UBO not identifiable exception path)
description: Exception path sequence for JRN-004 where the applicant's company has a corporate PSC (a holding company) that obscures the natural person beneficial owners. The bank is unable to identify the natural persons with >25% control through normal PSC data. This triggers the 'UBO not identifiable' exception (EX-B004). The MLRO (PER-052) is notified and the Relationship Manager (PER-050) coordinates enhanced UBO investigation. This is a failure-to-identify scenario, not a sanctions hit — the application is held pending additional information.

steps.description: Director of Holdco Ventures Ltd submits application: entity_type = limited_company, company_number = 99887766.
Application created. BusinessCustomer (prospect) and BusinessApplicationRecord created.

Companies House returns: company status = active, 1 director (Alice Pemberton), PSC = Holdco International BV (a Dutch company, 80% ownership). No natural person appears on the PSC register — the registered PSC is a foreign corporate entity.

Company verified as active. DirectorRecord created for Alice Pemberton. UBO staging records that the PSC is a corporate entity (Holdco International BV, Netherlands) — no natural person UBOs identifiable from PSC register.

data.payload: { legal_name: Holdco Ventures Ltd, company_status: active, director_count: 1, ubo_count_from_psc: 0, corporate_psc_detected: true, corporate_psc_name: Holdco International BV, corporate_psc_jurisdiction: NL }

steps.description: SVC-017 renders a specific prompt: 'One of your registered beneficial owners is itself a company (Holdco International BV). To comply with anti-money laundering regulations, we need to identify the individuals who ultimately own or control that company. Please provide: names, dates of birth, and nationalities of natural persons with >25% ownership of Holdco International BV; or a corporate structure chart. A Relationship Manager will contact you within 1 business day.'

steps.action: Applicant unable to provide UBO details online
steps.description: PER-002 states they cannot complete the corporate look-through online and requests RM assistance. Application transitions to AP-B002 (RM-assisted path) and EX-B004 (UBO not identifiable — investigation required).
SVC-005 publishes an internal exception event flagging that UBO identification cannot be completed via normal PSC data path. Application status set to 'pending_ubo_investigation'.

data.payload: { application_id, business_customer_id, exception_type: corporate_psc_look_through_required, corporate_psc: Holdco International BV, jurisdiction: NL }

steps.description: SVC-053 dispatches email to PER-002: 'We need additional information about the ownership structure of your company before we can proceed. A Relationship Manager will contact you within 1 business day. Your case reference is BCA-2025-00421. We aim to complete additional checks within 10 business days.'
steps.compliance_note: No mention of the specific AML concern — generic 'additional information' language only. Tipping-off prevention applied by analogy.

steps.description: SVC-014 raises an MLRO case for the corporate look-through requirement. MLRO case management system alert: 'UBO investigation required — corporate PSC (Netherlands). Application BCA-2025-00421, Holdco Ventures Ltd. Assigned to RM for document gathering.'

steps.action: CRM alert: RM assigned to case
steps.description: PER-050 (Relationship Manager) is assigned to the case. CRM alert: 'Holdco Ventures Ltd — UBO look-through required for Dutch corporate PSC. Please contact the customer and gather: corporate structure chart, names/DOB/nationality of natural persons with >25% ownership of Holdco International BV, or Dutch equivalent of Companies House extract.'

RM calls PER-002. Explains that the bank requires information about the individuals behind Holdco International BV. Requests: corporate structure chart, names/DOB/nationalities of UBOs, Dutch KvK extract or equivalent.
steps.note: RM interaction is off-system (telephone). Document upload via secure portal.

steps.description: PER-002 uploads: corporate structure chart showing Holdco International BV is 100% owned by two natural persons (Van den Berg family: Jan van den Berg 60%, Marieke van den Berg 40%). Dutch UBO register extract uploaded.

steps.action: RM uploads documents to MLRO case (Day 3)
steps.description: RM reviews uploaded documents, confirms they support the UBO identification claim, and submits the EDD package to the MLRO case.

MLRO reviews the corporate structure documentation. Jan van den Berg (60%) and Marieke van den Berg (40%) are confirmed as the natural person UBOs. Dutch UBO register extract is accepted as a reliable independent source. MLRO approves UBO identification. Two UltimateBeneficialOwner entities created in SVC-005 with control_type = shares and notes referencing the Dutch documentation.

steps.action: Publish UBOIdentified (x2 — Jan and Marieke van den Berg)
steps.description: SVC-005 publishes UBOIdentified for both confirmed natural person UBOs. Journey resumes at BPH-004 — identity verification invitations dispatched to Jan and Marieke van den Berg.

data.payload_example: { ubo_id, business_customer_id, ubo_first_name: Jan, ubo_last_name: van den Berg, ownership_percentage: 60.00, control_type: shares, jurisdiction: NL }

steps.action: Dispatch identity verification invitations to Jan and Marieke van den Berg
steps.description: SVC-050 dispatches secure verification invitation emails to both individuals. Journey now follows the normal BPH-004 path for the remaining verifications.

steps.action: In-app update: identity verification links sent
steps.description: SVC-017 updates the application status screen: 'We have identified the beneficial owners of your company. We have sent identity verification links to Jan van den Berg and Marieke van den Berg. Once both have completed their verification, we will proceed with your application.'

Alice Pemberton (director), Jan van den Berg (UBO), and Marieke van den Berg (UBO) complete identity verifications. DirectorVerified events published for each. Note: Dutch nationals require passport; Dutch address verification runs against EU credit bureau.
steps.note: Journey continues to BPH-005, BPH-006, BPH-007, BPH-008 via normal path — not shown here

outcome.notes: The UBO identification failure exception added approximately 3-4 business days to the standard 3-5 day SLA. The application ultimately proceeds to the normal BPH-005 through BPH-008 phases once the UBO documentation is accepted. If the applicant had been unable or unwilling to provide corporate structure documentation, the MLRO would have declined the application under MLR 2017 Regulation 21(3) (inability to complete CDD).
